## Overview

EuroSAT is a benchmark dataset of Sentinel-2 satellite image patches covering **10 land-use/land-cover classes** across Europe. This project applies classical machine learning and deep convolutional neural networks to classify land cover from both RGB and multispectral imagery.

**Classes:** Annual Crop · Forest · Herbaceous Vegetation · Highway · Industrial · Pasture · Permanent Crop · Residential · River · Sea/Lake

![](eurosat/eurosat_pic.png){.img-fluid style="border-radius:8px;"}

---

## 1. Data Loading & Exploration

- Loaded EuroSAT RGB patches (64×64 px) into NumPy arrays
- Explored class distribution and visualized one example per class
- Applied data augmentation before train/test split
- Created grayscale versions for traditional ML experiments

---

## 2. Traditional Machine Learning

Experiments restricted to **Forest, Residential, and Industrial** classes.

| Model | Approach |
|-------|----------|
| Binary SVMs | Three one-vs-one classifiers: Forest vs Residential, Forest vs Industrial, Residential vs Industrial |
| Multiclass SVM | Majority vote from the three binary classifiers |
| Random Forest | 300 estimators, all-CPU parallel, full multiclass |

---

## 3. Deep Learning

### 3.1 Fully Connected Networks (Grayscale)

Four architectures compared on flattened grayscale inputs:

| Model | Architecture |
|-------|-------------|
| Model 1 | Single-layer (input → softmax) |
| Model 2 | Two-layer NN |
| Model 3 | Four-layer NN with dropout |
| Ensemble | Probability averaging of Models 1–3 |

### 3.2 CNNs & Transfer Learning (RGB)

- **Model 4** — Custom CNN on RGB patches
- **Model 5** — MobileNetV2 transfer learning on RGB

Analyzed top confusion pairs and visualized misclassified examples.

### 3.3 Multispectral Transfer Learning

Extended the best RGB approach to full multispectral Sentinel-2 channels (>3 bands) using transfer learning adapted for multi-channel input.

---

## 4. Key Takeaways

- Transfer learning (MobileNetV2) outperformed custom CNNs on RGB data
- Spatial context from CNNs provided major gains over flattened grayscale inputs
- Multispectral channels carry additional discriminative signal beyond RGB
- Data augmentation before splitting helped generalization across all models
